title: Composition of the normalized mixed reduction units
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a scheme $W$, and finite coefficient fields $A\subseteq M\subseteq N$ in an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, allowing equality. Write $R_{B,n}=\mathcal O_B/(\varpi_B^{n+1})$, $n\geq0$, for $B=A,M,N$. Use the completed coefficient sheaves, coherent derived reduction $r_{B,n}$, and strict reduction towers of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Let $C_{B/D}$ be the specified completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and let $a:C_{N/M}C_{M/A}\cong C_{N/A}$ and $e:C_{A/A}\cong1$ be ordinary derived tensor associativity and multiplication transported by the quotient/zero-shifted-coordinate completion comparisons of [lem-pur-completed-line-tensor-coherence] (its scalar associator and unit, independent of the auxiliary lines). For a derived-complete object $K$ [def-weil-derived-complete], let $\eta_{B/D,n,K}:r_{D,n}K\to\operatorname{Res}_{R_{D,n}\to R_{B,n}}r_{B,n}(C_{B/D}K)$ be exactly the mixed completed reduction unit of [def-weil-mixed-reduction-unit], retaining its universal homotopy-category counit square and diagonal Roos normalization. Then, under the identity identification of successive scalar restrictions,
$$\operatorname{Res}_{A\to N}r_{N,n}(a_K)\circ\operatorname{Res}_{A\to M}(\eta_{N/M,n,C_{M/A}K})\circ\eta_{M/A,n,K}=\eta_{N/A,n,K},$$
$$r_{A,n}(e_K)\circ\eta_{A/A,n,K}=1_{r_{A,n}K}.$$
Here $\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B}$ in these formulas means restriction along $R_{A,n}\to R_{B,n}$. These are identities of the specified natural transformations of coherent reduction diagrams, induced with all quotient transitions by the entire homotopy-category normalization, and retained by their fixed strict-tower and derived-limit realizations. In particular the assertion includes the augmentation and both Roos coordinates. It is stronger than equality of cohomology maps or unrelated equalities after separate finite evaluation. No flatness of the quotient ring maps, finite Tor-amplitude condition on $K$, or choice of chain inverse for the completion maps is assumed.

proof.text: The canonical completed-to-sequence projection is obtained by SemilinearSections.quotientRingMap applied to the completed limit projections; limit.w proves their adjacent transition equations. Assemble the coefficient inclusions by NatTrans.ofOpSequence, using the quotient-transition square coefficientExtensionQuotient_naturality of [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model]. Uncurrying gives the morphism on the entire sequence site. Each map is unique by equality of every (n,U) component. For identity coefficients the quotient map is identity; for composition use quotient induction and functorial constant sheafification. Mathlib restrictScalarsId'App and restrictScalarsComp'App give the identity-on-sections restriction isomorphisms; sectionwise extensionality proves their uniqueness. These four construction claims are proved in Lean. The ordinary mixed unit and the following composition calculation remain to be proved. Write $B_{ji}$ for ordinary derived scalar extension, $C_{ji}$ for completed extension, $\chi_{ji}:B_{ji}\to C_{ji}$ for the prescribed completion map, $d:B_{21}B_{10}\to B_{20}$ for ordinary reassociation and $\lambda:B_{00}\to1$ for multiplication; indices $0,1,2$ mean $A,M,N$. Temporarily omit restrictions from notation, always restricting the final reduction to $R_{A,n}$. Let $v_{ji}$ be the ordinary mixed derived unit before completion in [def-weil-mixed-reduction-unit]. At the sheaf level its formula is $s\otimes x\mapsto i_{ji,n}(s)\otimes(1\otimes x)$. Thus two successive maps followed by reassociation send $s\otimes x$ to $i_{20,n}(s)\otimes(1\otimes x)$, and multiplication after the identity-field map sends $s\otimes x$ to itself. The uniqueness on sheafified tensors in that definition gives these equalities of sheaf transformations. Replacing $n+1$ by $n$ commutes with the formulas, because the quotient ring homomorphisms commute with coefficient inclusion. The same formulas degreewise therefore give equalities of transformations on complexes of entire quotient systems.

proof.text:
Use the ringed sequence model of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The scalar-extension adjoint of the ordinary mixed unit is the balanced comparison between the two words from the completed source ring to the target quotient ring: first source reduction then finite scalar extension, or first completed ordinary scalar extension then target reduction. Its formula is $(s\otimes x)\otimes t\mapsto i_{ji,n}(s)t\otimes(1\otimes x)$. Apply [lem-trf-ringed-kflat-word-comparison-descent] to these words on the sequence site: the same flat-term K-flat representative computes every word, and their universal counits uniquely descend all comparisons and pasting identities. Restriction is exact and the scalar adjunction has the insertion-of-one normalization by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Taking its adjoint therefore recovers exactly $v$ of [def-weil-mixed-reduction-unit], including its universal counit square. The pasting law of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clauses 1--2, identifies successive adjoints with the adjoint of the pasted balanced comparison. Thus step 1 descends to
$$r_2(d_K)v_{21,B_{10}K}v_{10,K}=v_{20,K},\qquad r_0(\lambda_K)v_{00,K}=1.$$
Here all reductions include restriction to $R_{A,n}$. The ordinary derived reassociation is the specified one of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. This establishes whole-system natural-transformation identities, with the representative computation counit equations; it never tests equality by separate evaluations. No flatness of the quotient maps is needed.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-quotient-scalar-comparison-descent], $\chi$ is a natural derived transformation on all inputs, descended from the quotient chain map with zero shifted-product coordinate. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], it is invertible on complete inputs and $B_{ji}K$ is complete there. Hence $C_{ji}K$, being isomorphic to $B_{ji}K$, is complete too: transport its completeness triangle by this isomorphism and the induced maps on reduction products. This verifies the completeness hypotheses for every comparison below. In particular $\chi_{21,B_{10}K}$ and $\chi_{21,C_{10}K}$ are invertible; there is no request for a chain inverse.

proof.text:
Set $t_K=C_{21}(\chi_{10,K})\circ\chi_{21,B_{10}K}$. The specified transport of ordinary associativity and multiplication in [lem-pur-completed-line-tensor-coherence] means exactly
$$a_K\circ t_K=\chi_{20,K}\circ d_K,\qquad e_K\circ\chi_{00,K}=\lambda_K.$$
Indeed its transported associator is $\chi_{20}d\,t^{-1}$ and its transported unitor is $\lambda\chi_{00}^{-1}$. The same node specifies that these $\chi$ are the quotient maps with zero shifted-product coordinate. No line or twist is used in these scalar equations.

proof.text:
By definition $\eta_{ji,K}=r_j(\chi_{ji,K})v_{ji,K}$, with restriction understood. Naturality of $v_{21}$ for $\chi_{10,K}$ and then naturality of $\chi_{21}$ give the typed identity
$$\begin{aligned}
\eta_{21,C_{10}K}\eta_{10,K}
&=r_2(\chi_{21,C_{10}K})\,v_{21,C_{10}K}\,r_1(\chi_{10,K})\,v_{10,K}\\
&=r_2(\chi_{21,C_{10}K}\circ B_{21}(\chi_{10,K}))\,v_{21,B_{10}K}\,v_{10,K}\\
&=r_2(C_{21}(\chi_{10,K})\circ\chi_{21,B_{10}K})\,v_{21,B_{10}K}\,v_{10,K}\\
&=r_2(t_K)\,v_{21,B_{10}K}\,v_{10,K}.
\end{aligned}$$
For example the middle naturality square has source $B_{21}B_{10}K$ and target $C_{21}C_{10}K$. All terms are restricted to $R_{A,n}$; successive restriction is literally restriction along the composite quotient homomorphism.

proof.text: Postcompose step 5 with $r_2(a_K)$. By step 4 its right side is $r_2(\chi_{20,K})r_2(d_K)v_{21,B_{10}K}v_{10,K}$, which step 2 identifies with $r_2(\chi_{20,K})v_{20,K}=\eta_{20,K}$. This is the first requested formula. For the repeated field, steps 4 and 2 give $r_0(e_K)\eta_{00,K}=r_0(e_K\chi_{00,K})v_{00,K}=r_0(\lambda_K)v_{00,K}=1$. The proof therefore includes equal adjacent fields and the two unit insertions, without replacing a completed identity-field functor by a strict identity.

proof.text: The equations in steps 2--6 are equations of whole-system transformations, and the completion maps used in them retain the prescribed augmentation and zero shifted-product coordinate. For a strict tower map $f$, the Roos map acts as $(y,x)\mapsto(\prod f_n(y),\prod f_n(x))$; composition with $g$ gives the diagonal map for $gf$. For a strict augmentation $\gamma$, this sends $(0,(\gamma_n)_n)$ to $(0,(f_n\gamma_n)_n)$. By [lem-pur-strict-roos-homotopy-functor] this is a functor on entire homotopy systems, including compatible homotopies, not just on their finite evaluations. Countable products are exact here by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Hence [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] gives its derived functor and its normalized natural comparison with total derived limit, carrying the zero-shifted-coordinate augmentation to the prescribed derived augmentation. Apply these functors to the established whole-system identities. This preserves the equalities with their fixed augmentations and both Roos coordinates; no equality of arbitrary chosen chain representatives or inference from limit projections is asserted. Completeness was used only to invert $\chi$ in the transported associator and unit.
